test.purpose: With a shallow branch listed first and a deep one second, the reported chain is the deep one in order — a search taking the first edge would give the wrong path and the wrong length.

test.name: depth_measures_from_the_deepest_entry_point
test.purpose: Given two entry points of different depths, the reported figure and chain are the worst case across them.

test.name: recursion_yields_no_depth_and_terminates
test.purpose: A recursive call graph reports its cycle, no depth figure, and no chain — and the run terminates, which a longest-path search over a cyclic graph would not.

test.name: no_entry_points_omits_depth_with_a_reason
test.purpose: With no declaration the depth analysis is omitted rather than failed, `main` is not inferred despite being present, and the measurements needing no declaration are still produced.

test.name: an_entry_point_matching_nothing_is_a_distinct_omission
test.purpose: A declared entry point naming no analysed function yields a different omission from declaring none, because the two call for different actions.

test.name: depth_carries_the_unresolved_count
test.purpose: The unresolved-call count travels with the depth, since a chain through an unresolved call is not followed and the figure is a lower bound.

test.name: a_chain_does_not_travel_along_a_global_edge
test.purpose: A chain stops at the last function actually called, rather than continuing to one that merely reads a global the callee wrote.

test.name: an_empty_project_measures_nothing_without_failing
test.purpose: A run that analysed nothing produces an empty but valid set of measurements.

test.name: tree_results_free_is_safe_on_null_and_twice
test.purpose: Releasing a null or already-released result set does not fault, so teardown is unconditional on every path.

test.name: excluded_extension_matches_the_runtime_list
test.purpose: An extension present in the runtime list is excluded and one absent from it is not, the list having been read from the runtime location rather than from any table in the binary.

test.name: excluded_extension_ignores_case
test.purpose: One entry covers every spelling of an extension, so a list maintained in lower case still excludes an upper-case file name.

test.name: a_name_without_an_extension_is_not_excluded
test.purpose: A dot occurring in a directory component, and a name that is nothing but a suffix, are both correctly read as having no extension to test.

test.name: an_empty_exclusion_list_excludes_nothing
test.purpose: An empty list excludes nothing, which is the state discovery runs in when the runtime file is absent.

test.name: extension_list_skips_comments_and_blank_lines
test.purpose: Comment and blank lines are not entries, and an entry written without its leading period still matches, so the data file can be maintained in either style.

test.name: a_missing_extension_list_is_not_fatal
test.purpose: An absent binary-extension file yields an empty list rather than aborting the run, so discovery still completes.

test.name: a_regular_file_target_is_appended_directly
test.purpose: A target that is a regular file is appended to the file list with no directory traversal performed for it.

test.name: a_missing_target_is_rejected_with_an_empty_list
test.purpose: A target that does not exist is rejected, and no partial file list survives the rejection.

test.name: a_target_that_is_neither_file_nor_directory_is_rejected
test.purpose: A FIFO named as a target is rejected, covering the class of targets that exist but are neither regular file nor directory.

test.name: every_target_is_validated_before_any_is_walked
test.purpose: A valid target given alongside an invalid one is not walked, so a report can never cover fewer targets than the user named.

test.name: a_file_reached_through_two_targets_appears_once
test.purpose: A file named explicitly and also contained in a named directory is retained once, canonicalisation having preceded de-duplication.

test.name: the_file_list_is_sorted_into_byte_order
test.purpose: The completed list is in ascending byte order whatever order the filesystem enumerated it in.

test.name: hidden_entries_and_binary_extensions_are_excluded
test.purpose: A hidden file, a hidden directory's contents, and a file carrying an excluded extension are all absent from the walk's result.

test.name: the_walk_descends_into_subdirectories
test.purpose: The traversal is recursive: a file several directories below the target is found.

test.name: a_hidden_directory_named_as_the_target_is_traversed
test.purpose: The hidden-entry exclusion applies below the target and not to the target itself, so a hidden directory named on the command line is walked.

test.name: files_and_directories_are_classified_independently
test.purpose: Each target is routed on its own type, so a file and a directory given together are both handled correctly.

test.name: a_cyclic_directory_symlink_terminates
test.purpose: A self-referential directory link does not produce an unbounded traversal, and the linked directory is not descended into. Reaching the assertion is itself the result.

test.name: a_symbolic_link_named_as_a_target_is_resolved
test.purpose: A link named directly as a target is resolved to its referent, the other half of the symbolic-link policy from the one the walk applies.

test.name: a_path_that_cannot_be_canonicalised_is_a_per_file_failure
test.purpose: A canonicalisation failure, provoked through a link-time wrapper, drops that path and records a per-file failure rather than ending the run.

test.name: git_walk_yields_the_tracked_files
test.purpose: The walk enumerates the files committed at `HEAD` and not a file that exists in the working tree but was never added, which is the exclusion the route exists to perform.

test.name: git_walk_is_scoped_to_the_target
test.purpose: Naming a subdirectory enumerates that subdirectory alone, though the tree at `HEAD` is the whole repository.

test.name: git_walk_declines_a_directory_in_no_repository
test.purpose: A directory outside any repository is declined rather than failed: nothing is appended, no failure is recorded, and the negative return is what sends the caller to the filesystem walk.

test.name: git_walk_declines_a_target_the_repository_does_not_track
test.purpose: A directory inside a work tree that `HEAD` knows nothing about — a build directory, or a home directory under version control — is declined, so the target is analysed by traversal instead of reported as empty.

test.name: a_tracked_directory_of_excluded_files_stays_on_the_git_route
test.purpose: A tracked directory whose every tracked file is excluded yields nothing and is still judged applicable, so the run does not fall back and analyse the untracked files beside them. Distinguishes "the repository tracks this directory" from "the repository yielded a file".

test.name: a_route_is_recorded_for_each_target
test.purpose: Each target's route is recorded in the order given, naming the same target twice records it once, and releasing the list leaves it usable rather than stale.

test.name: the_route_list_owns_the_target_it_records
test.purpose: Mutating the caller's buffer after recording does not change the record, so the report can outlive the strings discovery was given.

test.name: filelist_free_is_safe_on_null
test.purpose: Releasing a null file list or extension list does not fault, so teardown is safe on every path.

test.name: roots_are_entry_points_and_address_taken_functions
test.purpose: The root set is the union of the two and nothing else: a function neither declared nor address-taken is not a root.

test.name: a_declared_symbol_naming_nothing_is_skipped_not_fatal
test.purpose: A declared entry point matching no analysed function is skipped rather than failing the run, since analysing one directory of a project whose entry point lives in another is ordinary.

test.name: a_root_declared_twice_is_one_root
test.purpose: The root set is de-duplicated, so a symbol declared twice and also address-taken contributes one root.

test.name: a_clique_of_unused_functions_is_unreachable
test.purpose: Two unused functions calling one another are both reported: each has a caller, so a textual rule finds neither, and no path reaches the pair from any root.

test.name: an_address_taken_function_and_its_callees_are_reachable
test.purpose: An address-taken function is a root rather than an exemption: what it calls is reached through it. An implementation that merely excluded it from the report would report its callee dead.

test.name: reachability_does_not_travel_along_a_global_edge
test.purpose: A function reachable only by reading an object another function wrote is still unreachable: control never travels along a state edge, and following one would rescue genuinely dead code from the report.

test.name: with_no_entry_points_nothing_is_unreachable
test.purpose: With no declaration the analysis is omitted with its reason, and no function is reported unreachable.

test.name: a_declaration_matching_nothing_is_its_own_omission
test.purpose: Declaring an entry point that matches nothing is a different omission from declaring none, because the two call for different actions from the reader.

test.name: a_global_touched_by_one_function_is_a_scope_reduction_candidate
test.purpose: An object one function writes and reads is flagged, and the graph carries no edge for it at all — which is why the finding is computed from the access records rather than from the edge table.

test.name: a_global_spanning_disconnected_regions_is_a_hidden_channel
test.purpose: An object written in one region of the call graph and read in another that never calls it is flagged, with the region count establishing the disconnection.

test.name: shared_state_within_one_region_is_ordinary
test.purpose: The same sharing between two functions joined by a call edge carries no finding. Without this distinction the warning would fire on every shared variable.

test.name: an_undeclared_identifier_is_not_global_state
test.purpose: An identifier no file declares at file scope is not global state, however the over-broad read and write patterns captured it.

test.name: a_global_touched_only_by_dead_functions_is_unreachable
test.purpose: An object every one of whose accessors is unreachable is itself reported unreachable.

test.name: a_global_no_function_touches_is_not_claimed_dead
test.purpose: An object no analysed function accesses is not claimed: it may be touched from file scope or from a translation unit outside the target.

test.name: an_edge_crossing_a_declared_boundary_is_reported
test.purpose: A call from a function in one declared scope to a function in another is reported as a crossing.

test.name: a_shared_global_crossing_a_boundary_is_reported
test.purpose: A scope that never calls into another but writes a variable the other reads has not been isolated. An implementation checking call edges alone would report the arrangement clean.

test.name: a_component_matching_no_declaration_is_outside_the_partition
test.purpose: An edge touching a file no declaration names is not a crossing: inventing a boundary would report violations against a division nobody drew.

test.name: with_no_scopes_declared_the_analysis_is_omitted
test.purpose: With no execution scopes declared the analysis is omitted with its reason rather than reporting an empty result.

test.name: an_empty_graph_analyses_without_incident
test.purpose: A run that analysed nothing produces empty state results rather than faulting.

test.name: instability_is_ce_over_the_sum
test.purpose: Instability is efferent coupling divided by the sum of both couplings.

test.name: instability_is_zero_when_nothing_is_depended_upon
test.purpose: A component depending on nothing but depended upon widely is maximally stable, and the value is a real 0 rather than undefined — Ca is not zero, so the division is well formed.

test.name: instability_is_one_when_nothing_depends_on_it
test.purpose: The opposite extreme: freely changeable, because nothing rests on it.

test.name: instability_is_undefined_when_both_couplings_are_zero
test.purpose: No division is performed and the value is reported undefined. A component with no relationships at all is ordinary, and 0, 1 and NaN are all wrong answers for it.

test.name: coupling_counts_components_not_calls
test.purpose: Three calls into one component are one dependency. Counting call sites would treat a file calling another in forty places as depending on forty things.

test.name: a_call_within_one_component_is_no_coupling_at_all
test.purpose: A file does not depend on itself — the same rule that keeps intra-file recursion out of the cycle report.

test.name: a_bottleneck_needs_both_couplings_at_the_threshold
test.purpose: A component is flagged only where afferent and efferent coupling each meet the threshold; a widely-used leaf is stable, not a bottleneck.

test.name: a_cycle_between_two_components_is_found_with_a_loop
test.purpose: The group and a concrete loop through it are both produced, since the group is what must be broken up and the loop is which edge to cut.

test.name: mutual_recursion_within_one_component_is_not_a_cycle
test.purpose: The case HLR-083 names. The call view holds a cycle and the component projection does not, so reporting it would tell an architect to split a file over a function-level recursion finding.

test.name: an_acyclic_projection_yields_no_cycles
test.purpose: A one-directional dependency between two components is not a cycle.

test.name: a_three_component_cycle_reports_its_whole_group
test.purpose: A longer cycle reports every member and a loop visiting all three.

test.name: a_call_descending_two_layers_is_skip_level_only
test.purpose: Bypassing an intervening layer in the declared direction is skip-level and inverts nothing.

test.name: a_call_ascending_one_layer_is_inverted_only
test.purpose: Running against the declared direction without bypassing anything is direction-inverted and is not a skip.

test.name: a_call_ascending_two_layers_is_both
test.purpose: Both statements are true of such a call and each has its own remedy, so it is reported twice rather than folded into one finding.

test.name: a_call_descending_one_layer_is_no_violation
test.purpose: The arrangement the user declared produces nothing. Without this an implementation flagging every inter-layer call would pass every test above.

test.name: a_component_in_no_declared_stratum_is_outside_the_partition
test.purpose: A file no declaration names has nothing to be compared against; placing it would report violations against a design nobody drew.

test.name: with_no_strata_declared_layering_is_omitted
test.purpose: The layering is omitted with its reason, and the coupling table is produced all the same.

test.name: a_state_edge_is_not_a_layering_violation
test.purpose: A global two layers share is a different fact with its own analyses; the dependency is still counted in the coupling table.

test.name: an_empty_graph_analyses_without_incident
test.purpose: A run that analysed nothing produces empty architectural results rather than faulting.

test.name: the_fan_out_bands_match_the_published_table
test.purpose: Each of the eight boundary values from PVD Appendix A.2 bands as the table says. The same eight are pinned as measurements by calltree/fanout.c, so a disagreement here is a banding error rather than a counting one.

test.name: the_acceptable_band_produces_no_finding
test.purpose: A fan-out of 9 is acceptable and silent. This band was a gap in an earlier reading of the thresholds, which is why exhaustiveness is stated rather than inferred.

test.name: every_fan_out_value_classifies_exactly_once
test.purpose: Exhaustiveness as a property rather than as cases: every value from 0 to 40 lands in exactly one band, with none skipped and none claimed twice.

test.name: every_catalogued_measurement_names_a_source
test.purpose: Every row of the catalogue carries a non-empty attribution. A row without one would be an opinion elc held and did not admit to.

test.name: exactly_one_threshold_is_elcs_own_and_says_so
test.purpose: Exactly one threshold is not a published standard, it is the bottleneck, and its text says so where a reader sees it. Asserting the count means a second could only appear by decision rather than by drift.

test.name: the_published_thresholds_are_not_marked_as_elcs_own
test.purpose: The published rows cite MISRA and Martin and carry no elc marker, so the label distinguishes rather than decorating everything.

test.name: a_kind_outside_the_catalogue_yields_no_entry
test.purpose: A measurement kind the catalogue does not hold returns no entry, so the caller reports a bare value rather than discarding it or inventing a band.

test.name: the_severity_set_is_closed_and_ordered
test.purpose: The three names are exactly the closed set, and their ranks order info below warning below critical — the ordering that 'the highest applicable band wins' is defined against.

test.name: an_unrecognised_severity_ranks_lowest_rather_than_faulting
test.purpose: A name outside the set, and a null one, rank lowest instead of faulting the ordering.

test.name: the_highest_applicable_band_is_the_one_reported
test.purpose: A value above both bounds produces one finding at the higher severity, not two findings or the lower one.

test.name: every_finding_carries_exactly_one_severity
test.purpose: No finding is emitted without a severity, and none carries a value outside the closed set.

test.name: call_depth_bands_at_eight_and_twelve
test.purpose: Depth bands against the embedded guidance: 8 is within it, 9 warns, 12 warns, 13 is critical.

test.name: an_omitted_depth_is_not_banded_as_zero
test.purpose: A depth omitted for want of an entry point is not banded at all. Banding it would judge a number that does not exist.

test.name: a_clean_project_yields_no_findings
test.purpose: Finding nothing is an ordinary result. Paired with every band test so that an implementation emitting findings unconditionally cannot pass them.

test.name: findinglist_free_is_safe_on_null_and_twice
test.purpose: Releasing an empty or already-released finding list does not fault.

test.name: every_discovered_function_becomes_a_node
test.purpose: Every function across every analysed file receives a node, so the graph spans the project rather than any one file.

test.name: node_identifiers_follow_sorted_file_order
test.purpose: Files handed over in unsorted order still number their functions by sorted path, so node identifiers are a property of the source tree and not of discovery order.

test.name: a_call_resolves_across_files
test.purpose: A call whose definition lies in another file resolves to an edge, which is the cross-file resolution the graph exists to perform.

test.name: repeated_calls_collapse_to_one_edge_with_a_count
test.purpose: Three call sites between one pair of functions produce one edge carrying a count of three, so out-degree is distinct callees rather than call sites.

test.name: an_unresolvable_call_is_counted_and_does_not_abort
test.purpose: A call into a library is counted, produces no edge, and does not fail the build — no destination is invented for it, which is what keeps a later dead-code proof sound.

test.name: a_call_from_file_scope_has_no_caller_node
test.purpose: A call outside every reported function draws no edge and is counted as unresolved, because the graph does not represent it and the reader is judging completeness.

test.name: a_global_links_its_writer_to_its_reader
test.purpose: A global written in one file and read in another produces an edge between the two functions, and that edge names the object through the graph's own copy of the string.

test.name: an_undeclared_name_is_not_global_state
test.purpose: An identifier written in one function and read in another, declared nowhere at file scope, produces no edge — the over-broad capture is resolved away rather than believed.

test.name: two_objects_between_one_pair_are_two_edges
test.purpose: Global edges are per object and do not collapse the way call edges do, since merging them would lose which shared state couples the two functions.

test.name: an_address_taken_function_is_marked
test.purpose: A function assigned without being called is marked as a reachability root, captured in this phase though Phase 10 is what consumes it.

test.name: an_address_taken_name_that_is_not_a_function_is_discarded
test.purpose: An ordinary variable captured by the deliberately over-broad address-taken patterns resolves to nothing and marks no node, which is what allows the query files not to decide.

test.name: the_component_projection_is_file_level
test.purpose: A call between functions in two files yields one component edge between those files, a component being a source file.

test.name: a_call_within_one_file_is_no_component_dependency
test.purpose: A call inside one file adds no component edge, so a file is not recorded as depending on itself.

test.name: an_empty_project_builds_an_empty_graph
test.purpose: A run that analysed nothing builds a valid empty graph, including the library structure, rather than failing or leaving a null handle.

test.name: the_library_returns_errors_instead_of_aborting
test.purpose: Asking a cyclic graph for a topological ordering returns an error rather than aborting the process, so the library's default abort-on-error handler has been replaced. Reaching the assertion is itself the result: without the handler the test dies rather than fails.

test.name: graph_free_is_safe_on_null_and_twice
test.purpose: Releasing a null or an already-released graph does not fault, so teardown is unconditional on every exit path.

test.name: dot_is_written_without_being_asked_for
test.purpose: A zeroed ElcOptions with an output path warrants the companion: generation is enabled by default, which is the one place the `.dot` default runs opposite to GraphML's.

test.name: dot_is_suppressed_by_the_disable_switch
test.purpose: The disable switch turns the default off.

test.name: dot_needs_an_output_path
test.purpose: With the report going to standard output nothing is warranted, there being no path to derive the companion's name from.

test.name: dot_needs_an_output_path_even_when_disabled
test.purpose: "Whether or not generation was disabled" is the requirement's wording: the destination decides it and the switch cannot change the answer, so both paths are asserted rather than one.

test.name: no_dot_is_written_from_a_saved_record
test.purpose: A record carries the findings of a run rather than the topology they were drawn from, so regeneration warrants no companion even with an output path and the default in force.

test.name: graphml_is_off_unless_asked_for
test.purpose: With an output path but no request, no export is warranted: the export is opt-in, unlike the .dot companion.

test.name: graphml_needs_an_output_path
test.purpose: With the export requested but the report going to standard output, nothing is warranted — there is no path to derive the companion's name from.

test.name: graphml_is_written_when_asked_for_and_named
test.purpose: Both conditions together warrant the export.

test.name: the_companion_replaces_the_extension
test.purpose: report.md yields report.graphml rather than report.md.graphml: the extension is substituted, not appended.

test.name: a_path_without_an_extension_gains_one
test.purpose: An output path with no extension gains the companion's rather than being left unnamed.

test.name: a_dot_in_a_directory_is_not_an_extension
test.purpose: A dot in a directory name is not mistaken for the file's extension, which would otherwise truncate the path at the directory.

test.name: a_directory_dot_with_an_extension_still_substitutes
test.purpose: A dotted directory alongside a real extension substitutes the extension and leaves the directory alone.

test.name: both_companions_derive_from_one_output_path
test.purpose: One derivation serves both artefacts, which is what makes it impossible for either to take an output path of its own.

test.name: totals_sum_across_every_file
test.purpose: The project totals are the sum of the per-file physical line counts across every analysed file.

test.name: files_are_presented_in_ascending_path_order
test.purpose: Files are ordered by path in the model, so presentation order is a property of the report rather than of the order the files were discovered.

test.name: an_empty_run_yields_a_complete_model_with_zero_totals
test.purpose: A run in which no file was analysed still produces a complete model with zero totals, which renders normally.

test.name: assembly_leaves_the_accumulator_empty
test.purpose: Ownership of the per-file metrics moves into the report, so releasing both the accumulator and the report cannot free the same metrics twice.

test.name: a_failed_growth_leaves_the_accumulator_intact
test.purpose: A reallocation failure, provoked through a link-time wrapper, is reported and leaves the original allocation intact rather than overwriting it with a null pointer.

test.name: free_is_safe_on_null
test.purpose: Releasing a null report or accumulator does not fault, so teardown is safe on every path.

test.name: the_table_carries_the_summary_and_every_file
test.purpose: The rendered table contains the project summary tier and one row for each file in the model.

test.name: columns_are_aligned_on_the_longest_path
test.purpose: Every file row is rendered to the same width, the path column having been sized from the longest path in the model.

test.name: an_empty_report_still_renders_a_table
test.purpose: A model with no files still renders its headings and column rule, so an empty run is distinguishable from a crash.

test.name: a_write_failure_is_reported
test.purpose: A stream that cannot absorb the report yields a non-zero return, so a truncated report is never reported as success.

test.name: --help exits 0
test.purpose: Requesting help succeeds; it is not an error.

trace.name: Help Request Is Not an Error

test.name: -h exits 0
test.purpose: The short form of the help option behaves as the long form.

trace.name: Help Request Is Not an Error

test.name: --help writes the summary to stdout, not stderr
test.purpose: The help summary goes to the results stream and nothing goes to the diagnostic stream.

trace.name: Help Request Is Not an Error
Diagnostics on stderr, Results on stdout

test.name: --help lists every option elc accepts
test.purpose: The usage summary names each accepted option, making it the reference the documentation is checked against.

trace.name: Help Request Is Not an Error

test.name: HLR-103: --help documents the switch that declines the call tree
test.purpose: The usage summary is the reference the documentation is checked against, so an option that parses must also print; without this the documentation test would compare two documents against a table missing an entry.

test.name: --help documents the exit-status scheme
test.purpose: The usage summary describes what each exit status means.

trace.name: Help Request Is Not an Error

test.name: --help is reported without validating other arguments
test.purpose: A help request short-circuits argument validation.

trace.name: Help Request Is Not an Error

test.name: an unrecognised long option exits 2
test.purpose: An unrecognised long option terminates with the fatal status.

test.name: an unrecognised short option exits 2
test.purpose: An unrecognised short option terminates with the fatal status.

test.name: no target exits 2
test.purpose: An invocation with no target terminates with the fatal status.

test.name: a usage error writes to stderr, not stdout
test.purpose: A usage error writes its diagnostic and summary to the diagnostic stream, leaving the results stream empty.

trace.name: Diagnostics on stderr, Results on stdout

test.name: a usage error names the offending option
test.purpose: The diagnostic identifies which option was rejected.

test.name: no target is diagnosed explicitly
test.purpose: The missing-target case is diagnosed in its own words rather than as a generic failure.

test.name: a single target is accepted
test.purpose: A single file target is accepted.

test.name: several targets are accepted, files and directories intermixed
test.purpose: Several targets are accepted in one invocation, files and directories freely mixed.

test.name: HLR-103: --no-dot is accepted and takes no argument
test.purpose: The option parses as a flag rather than swallowing the target that follows it.

test.name: an accepted invocation writes its report to stdout
test.purpose: Nothing but results reaches the results stream.

trace.name: Diagnostics on stderr, Results on stdout

test.name: a decoy dotfile in the working directory changes nothing
test.purpose: Configuration-like files planted beside the invocation produce byte-identical output to their absence.

test.name: the man page exists
test.purpose: The project delivers a man page.

test.name: the user manual exists
test.purpose: The project delivers a user manual.

test.purpose: The delivered man page is well-formed roff.

test.name: the usage summary advertises at least one option
test.purpose: The reference the documentation is checked against is non-empty.

test.name: every option in the usage summary appears in the man page
test.purpose: No accepted option is undocumented in the man page.

trace.name: Documentation Updated With the Behaviour It Describes

test.name: every option in the usage summary appears in the user manual
test.purpose: No accepted option is undocumented in the user manual.

trace.name: Documentation Updated With the Behaviour It Describes

test.name: every long option the man page documents is accepted by elc
test.purpose: No documented option is unimplemented.

trace.name: Documentation Updated With the Behaviour It Describes

test.name: both documents describe the exit-status scheme
test.purpose: Both documents describe the exit-status classes.

test.name: a directory target prints a table of its files
test.purpose: A directory target produces the aligned table, listing the files found beneath it.

test.name: the table reports physical line counts
test.purpose: The project total is the sum of the physical line counts of the files discovered.

test.name: a single file target reports that file alone
test.purpose: A regular-file target reports that file and performs no traversal for it.

test.name: files and directories may be intermixed on one command line
test.purpose: Files and directories given together are each classified on their own type and combined into one report.

test.name: the output shape does not depend on the type of the target
test.purpose: A file target and a directory target produce the same headings and the same columns, so results from different target types are directly comparable.

test.name: a file named alongside a directory containing it is counted once
test.purpose: A file reached through two overlapping targets appears exactly once in the report and once in the totals.

test.name: two runs over the same target are byte-identical
test.purpose: Repeating an unmodified run produces identical bytes.

test.name: targets given in a different order produce identical output
test.purpose: The order the targets were named in does not show through into the report.

test.name: a target that does not exist exits 2
test.purpose: An absent target ends the run with the status reserved for a run that never happened.

test.name: a target that is neither a file nor a directory exits 2
test.purpose: A FIFO named as a target is rejected, covering the class of targets that exist but are of the wrong type.

test.name: an unreadable target exits 2
test.purpose: A target that exists but cannot be read is rejected before any analysis, rather than becoming a per-file failure part-way through.

test.name: an invalid target produces no report at all
test.purpose: A valid target given alongside an invalid one yields no output, so no report can silently cover fewer targets than were named.

test.name: an invalid target is diagnosed on stderr, naming it
test.purpose: The diagnostic identifies the offending target and reaches the diagnostic stream, not the results stream.

test.name: a target with no files reports zero totals and exits 0
test.purpose: A run that found nothing to analyse still emits a well-formed report with zero totals and succeeds.

test.name: the report goes to stdout and nothing else does
test.purpose: A successful run writes its results to standard output and writes nothing to standard error.

test.name: --output writes the report to the named file
test.purpose: The report is written to the named file, and standard output is left empty.

test.name: -o is the short form of --output
test.purpose: The short form of the redirection option behaves as the long form.

test.name: a redirected report is byte-identical to the one on stdout
test.purpose: Redirection changes where the report goes, not what it says.

test.name: an output file that cannot be opened exits 2
test.purpose: A destination that cannot be opened ends the run with the status reserved for a run that produced no report.

test.name: an output file that cannot be opened is diagnosed on stderr
test.purpose: The diagnostic names the destination and reaches the diagnostic stream.

test.name: an unreadable file inside a target degrades the run to 1
test.purpose: A file within a target that cannot be read is a per-file failure: the report still covers the files that succeeded, and the exit status says so.

test.name: HLR-007: the language is determined from the extension, unprompted
test.purpose: A file's language is detected from its extension with no user declaration, and is shown in the report.

test.name: HLR-007: a header is detected as well as a source file
test.purpose: A header maps to a language and its definitions are reported, so a project's headers are not silently uncovered.

test.name: HLR-008: files sharing a language are analysed in one invocation
test.purpose: Several files are analysed in a single invocation and a single pass, with no per-language re-invocation.

test.name: HLR-014: each function is reported with its name and line range
test.purpose: Every function discovered is reported with its name and its start and end lines.

test.name: HLR-014: the line range starts at the signature, not the brace
test.purpose: The reported span begins where a reader says the function begins, rather than at the body's opening delimiter.

test.name: HLR-033: functions are presented in start-line order
test.purpose: Functions appear in start-line order rather than in the order the query happened to match them.

test.name: HLR-012: a file with no language module is listed as skipped
test.purpose: A file whose extension maps to no language appears in the report's skipped list, so the report accounts for every discovered file.

test.name: HLR-012: a skipped file is also reported on stderr
test.purpose: The skip is reported through both observables the requirement names: the list and a diagnostic.

test.name: HLR-037: a skip does not make the exit status non-zero
test.purpose: A skipped file is not a failure and does not by itself make the status non-zero.

test.name: HLR-012: a skipped file does not contribute to the totals
test.purpose: A skipped file is accounted for without being counted: the project totals are unchanged by its presence.

test.name: HLR-035: a file that fails to parse does not abort the run
test.purpose: A file that fails to parse leaves the rest of the run intact and the report covers the files that succeeded.

test.name: HLR-120: a parse failure degrades the run to 1
test.purpose: A parse failure produces the status reserved for a run that completed but did not process every file.

test.name: HLR-035: a parse failure names the file on stderr
test.purpose: The diagnostic identifies the file that failed and reaches the diagnostic stream.

test.name: HLR-019: each file reports its own line and function counts
test.purpose: Each file's row carries its own physical line count and the number of functions it defines.

test.name: HLR-066: a target of only skipped files still reports zero totals
test.purpose: A run in which nothing could be analysed still emits a well-formed report with zero totals, and names what it skipped.

test.name: HLR-006: the report has the same sections whatever the target type
test.purpose: A file target and a directory target produce the same sections in the same order.

test.name: HLR-015: each function reports its own ELOC
test.purpose: A function's own ELOC appears beside its line range.

test.name: HLR-024: the project summary carries a combined ELOC total
test.purpose: The summary reports the combined ELOC across every analysed file.

test.name: HLR-025: the totals are broken down by language
test.purpose: The report carries a per-language section, so each language's contribution is separately visible.

test.name: HLR-025: the per-language totals sum to the project totals
test.purpose: With one language present, its row equals the summary exactly — the breakdown is a partition of the totals, not a second count of them.

test.name: HLR-019: a header of declarations only reports zero ELOC
test.purpose: A file's own line and ELOC counts are reported per file, and a header whose only statement is one return reports one.

test.name: HLR-032: two runs over a parsed tree are byte-identical
test.purpose: Repeating a run that parses produces identical bytes, so the new sections are as deterministic as the old ones.

test.name: HLR-011: five languages are detected from their extensions
test.purpose: One target holding a file of each delivered language yields all five in the per-language breakdown.

test.name: HLR-008: a mixed-language target is analysed in one invocation
test.purpose: Four languages are analysed in a single pass, with every function found — no invocation per language.

test.name: HLR-025: each language's contribution is separately visible
test.purpose: A two-language target reports both languages, in name order.

test.name: HLR-011: elc requires no particular language to be present
test.purpose: A target of one language runs exactly as a mixed one does; nothing verifies that the other four are installed.

test.name: HLR-035: a file with a syntax error is measured around it
test.purpose: The report covers the functions the grammar could follow in a damaged file. This asserted the opposite until a real project showed that the discard-everything rule cost half its metrics.

test.name: HLR-035: the damage is reported beside the figures it qualifies
test.purpose: The safety property that makes measuring a damaged file acceptable: the file is named in a section of its own and the unparsed total appears in the summary, so a partial measurement never reads as a complete one.

test.name: HLR-035: an undamaged run says so, with nothing in the section
test.purpose: The summary reports zero unparsed lines and the section is empty for a sound run, so the damage reporting has to be earned.

test.name: HLR-035: the diagnostic gives the line, the scale, and what was kept
test.purpose: The stderr diagnostic names the line the damage begins at, how many lines it spans, and that the remainder was measured. "Parse error; file skipped" withheld the scale, which on a file damaged in one line reads far worse than it is.

test.name: HLR-017: complexity is reported per function
test.purpose: Each function's complexity appears beside its ELOC: one for a function that never branches, four for one that branches three times.

test.name: HLR-026: the summary names the most complex function and the largest file
test.purpose: The report carries both project-wide callouts, naming the function and the file.

test.name: HLR-022: the threshold defaults to 15
test.purpose: With no option given, the listing is built at the documented default.

test.name: HLR-021: a function at or over the threshold is listed for its file
test.purpose: A function meeting the threshold appears in the per-file listing, against the file that defines it.

test.name: HLR-021: the listing is at-or-over, not strictly over
test.purpose: A function whose complexity equals the threshold is listed; one below it is not. The boundary is the requirement's word, and an off-by-one here is invisible in any other test.

test.name: HLR-022: a lower threshold lists more
test.purpose: Lowering the threshold enlarges the listing, so the option reaches the listing at all.

test.name: HLR-063: a malformed threshold is a usage error
test.purpose: An argument that is not a number is rejected with the usage-error status rather than silently becoming some other threshold.

test.name: HLR-023: the threshold does not affect the exit status
test.purpose: A threshold every function breaches and one no function breaches both exit 0. Findings are data; deciding what a number warrants is the caller's.

test.name: HLR-023: the threshold changes the listing and nothing else
test.purpose: Everything above the listing section is byte-identical at two very different thresholds, so no total, callout, or ordering moves with it.

test.name: HLR-023: the threshold does not change the totals or the callouts
test.purpose: A threshold no function meets leaves the function count and the callouts as they were — the report still describes the code.

test.name: HLR-026: a tie for most complex resolves the same way every run
test.purpose: Two functions of equal complexity resolve to the one sorting first under the presentation order, identically on every run.

test.name: HLR-032: two runs with a threshold are byte-identical
test.purpose: Repeating a run with a threshold produces identical bytes.

test.name: HLR-066: an empty run still renders the callouts and the listing
test.purpose: A run that analysed nothing renders both new sections with no rows, rather than omitting them and changing the report's shape.

test.name: an_ordinary_field_is_not_quoted
test.purpose: A field needing no escape is emitted bare, so the common case stays readable rather than uniformly quoted.

test.name: a_field_containing_a_comma_is_quoted
test.purpose: A comma is what separates fields, so a value carrying one is quoted — the template-signature case, where one identifier looks like two fields.

test.name: a_quote_is_doubled_not_backslashed
test.purpose: RFC 4180 escapes a quote by doubling it. A backslash escape parses without error and carries the wrong text, which is worse than failing.

test.name: a_field_containing_a_newline_is_quoted
test.purpose: A line break inside a field ends the record unless the field is quoted.

test.name: a_field_containing_a_carriage_return_is_quoted
test.purpose: Records are CRLF-terminated, so a carriage return ends one as surely as a newline.

test.name: a_field_needing_every_escape_survives
test.purpose: A comma, a quote, and a newline in one field are handled together rather than one rule cancelling another.

test.name: an_empty_field_is_emitted_empty
test.purpose: An empty value is an empty field.

test.name: a_null_field_is_emitted_empty
test.purpose: A missing value is an empty field rather than a fault, so a record with an absent language still has the right shape.

test.name: the_header_row_is_written
test.purpose: The header names the columns each record carries, and passes through the same emission path as every record.

test.name: an_empty_report_is_a_header_alone
test.purpose: A run with no functions produces the header and nothing else, rather than no output at all.

test.name: a_write_failure_is_reported
test.purpose: A stream that cannot absorb the document yields a non-zero return, so a truncated file is never reported as success.

test.name: an_ampersand_is_escaped
test.purpose: An unescaped ampersand begins an entity reference and makes the document unparseable.

test.name: angle_brackets_are_escaped
test.purpose: An angle bracket would open or close a tag — the template-signature case, which carries both.

test.name: quotation_marks_are_escaped
test.purpose: A quotation mark inside an attribute value ends the attribute early, leaving the document unparseable from that point.

test.name: an_ampersand_in_an_entity_is_escaped_once
test.purpose: Escaping is not recursive: text that already looks like an entity is encoded once, not doubled.

test.name: ordinary_text_is_unchanged
test.purpose: A value needing no escape passes through untouched.

test.name: escaping_null_emits_nothing
test.purpose: A missing value emits nothing rather than faulting.

test.name: the_record_carries_its_format_version
test.purpose: The root element carries a format-version identifier, which is what lets a consumer decide whether it understands the structure before interpreting it.

test.name: an_empty_report_is_still_a_complete_record
test.purpose: A run that analysed nothing still writes a complete, well-formed record rather than nothing.

test.name: a_write_failure_is_reported
test.purpose: A truncated record is not well-formed and a consumer would reject it with no idea why, so a write failure is reported instead.

test.name: input_that_is_not_xml_is_rejected
test.purpose: A file that is not XML at all is rejected.

test.name: well_formed_but_foreign_input_is_rejected
test.purpose: A well-formed document of some other shape is rejected outright, with nothing reconstructed from it.

test.name: an_unsupported_format_version_is_rejected
test.purpose: A record of a version this build does not read is rejected rather than interpreted optimistically.

test.name: a_record_without_a_version_is_rejected
test.purpose: A record with no version identifier is rejected: the identifier is what makes the structure knowable.

test.name: the_threshold_supplied_now_is_the_one_applied
test.purpose: One record read at two thresholds yields two different listings, so the threshold is the one supplied at conversion time and the record carries none.

test.name: the_model_is_reconstructed_from_the_record
test.purpose: The model is rebuilt from the record alone, ordered by the same code that orders a live one, with the totals recomputed rather than read.

test.name: a_truncated_record_is_rejected
test.purpose: A record whose root never closes is not well-formed and is rejected rather than read as far as it goes.

test.name: an_absent_record_is_rejected
test.purpose: A record that cannot be opened is a rejection rather than a crash.

test.name: HLR-027: table is the format when none is selected
test.purpose: The aligned table is what a run with no format option produces.

test.name: HLR-027: table may also be selected explicitly
test.purpose: Selecting the default explicitly produces the same bytes as not selecting it.

test.name: HLR-028: csv produces one record per function
test.purpose: CSV carries a header and a record naming each function.

test.name: HLR-029: md produces GitHub-Flavored Markdown
test.purpose: Markdown carries headings and pipe tables rather than the aligned form.

test.name: HLR-054: xml produces a record with a version
test.purpose: XML carries a closed root element with a format-version identifier.

test.name: HLR-063: an unknown format is a usage error naming the choices
test.purpose: An unrecognised format is rejected, and the diagnostic names what would have been accepted.

test.name: HLR-063: a format option without its argument is a usage error
test.purpose: An option requiring an argument and given none is rejected.

test.name: HLR-031: table and Markdown present the same tiers
test.purpose: The two formats emit the same headings in the same order, which is the observable form of their sharing one traversal.

test.name: HLR-031: a tier with no rows appears in both
test.purpose: A tier that happens to be empty is still present in both formats, so the report's shape does not vary with its content.

test.name: the format changes the rendering and not the analysis
test.purpose: Every format names the same discovered function, so the formats are views of one run rather than four separate reports.

test.name: HLR-028: csv is unfiltered by the threshold
test.purpose: Two very different thresholds produce identical CSV: the threshold governs a listing tier CSV does not have.

test.name: HLR-054: xml is unfiltered by the threshold
test.purpose: The record stores what was measured, so the threshold does not change it.

test.name: HLR-038: every format writes results to stdout alone
test.purpose: Each format leaves the diagnostic stream carrying only diagnostics.

test.name: HLR-030: every format honours --output
test.purpose: Redirection applies to every format, not only the default one.

test.name: HLR-032: every format is byte-identical across runs
test.purpose: Repeating a run in any format produces identical bytes.

test.name: HLR-066: every format renders an empty run
test.purpose: A run that analysed nothing still produces output in every format.

test.name: the hand-counted category totals match
test.purpose: The physical line count, the file's ELOC, and the function count match the values counted line by line in the fixture's header.

test.name: HLR-015: the function's ELOC excludes the file-scope statement
test.purpose: The function reports eighteen of the file's nineteen statement lines; the nineteenth is an initialised global outside it.

test.name: HLR-019: the file's ELOC includes code outside any function
test.purpose: The file's ELOC accounts for every qualifying line, including the one that belongs to no function.

test.name: HLR-049 – HLR-052: blanks, braces, bare declarations and directives are excluded
test.purpose: The fixture holds two directives, three bare declarations, five lone braces and six blank lines; counting any of them would exceed the hand count.

test.name: HLR-017: the hand-counted complexity matches
test.purpose: The function's complexity matches the value counted by hand in the fixture's header: one plus five decision points.

test.name: HLR-017: a straight-line function is one
test.purpose: A function with no branch reports one, not two — the base is added once, and the query does not capture the function itself.

test.name: HLR-017: a short-circuit operator is a decision point
test.purpose: A `&&` inside a condition adds a decision, so a function built from one compound condition does not score as though it had none.

test.name: HLR-017: a default label and a goto are not decisions
test.purpose: A `default` label adds no path that was not already counted and a `goto` chooses nothing, so neither raises the complexity.

test.name: HLR-044: an assignment or operation counts
test.purpose: An initialising declaration, a plain assignment, and a compound operation each contribute a line.

test.name: HLR-046: a call counts whether or not its result is used
test.purpose: A call whose result is discarded counts as surely as one whose result is used; the prototypes beside them declare and do nothing.

test.name: HLR-047: a return counts, with or without a value
test.purpose: A bare return and a return carrying a value each contribute a line.

test.name: HLR-045: else-if on one line counts once
test.purpose: A line that is both an else and an if contributes one line, since ELOC counts lines rather than captures.

test.name: HLR-020: a file with nothing executable reports zero, without error
test.purpose: A file of comments, directives, and declarations reports zero ELOC and succeeds.

test.name: HLR-011: C++ matches its hand-counted categories
test.purpose: C++'s ELOC and complexity match the values counted line by line in the group's header, over a fixture holding one instance of every category the language has.

test.name: HLR-011: Python matches its hand-counted categories
test.purpose: Python's figures match its hand count, including the decisions the query file records: `pass` and `import` excluded, the module docstring counted as the expression statement it is.

test.name: HLR-011: Rust matches its hand-counted categories
test.purpose: Rust's figures match its hand count, including a counted `static` against an excluded `const`, and a tail expression counted where the language has no `return`.

test.name: HLR-011: Ada matches its hand-counted categories
test.purpose: Ada's figures match its hand count, including short-circuit `and then` counted as a decision where plain `and` is not.

test.name: HLR-048: C++ counts exception handling toward ELOC
test.purpose: The one ELOC category C cannot express. `try`, `catch`, and `throw` each contribute a line, which no earlier phase could verify in any shipped language.

test.name: HLR-048: a catch clause is a decision point
test.purpose: A handler is a path out of the guarded block and raises complexity; `try` and `throw` choose nothing and do not.

test.name: HLR-011: a language with no exception construct still reports
test.purpose: C has no exception handling and analysing it is not thereby an error — no language is required to have every category.

test.name: the hand-counted comment totals match
test.purpose: The physical line count, the file's ELOC, and the function count match the fixture's hand-counted header.

test.name: HLR-013: a block-comment opener inside a string opens nothing
test.purpose: A string containing a block-comment opener is a string. A textual matcher would open a comment there and swallow the rest of the file.

test.name: HLR-013: a line-comment opener inside a string discards nothing
test.purpose: A string containing a line-comment opener is a string. A textual matcher would discard the rest of that line, losing a statement.

test.name: HLR-013: a quote inside a comment opens no string
test.purpose: An unbalanced quote inside a comment opens nothing. A matcher tracking strings textually would mis-read everything after it — the case no regular expression survives, and the reason HLR-013's verification is bound to this group.

test.name: HLR-016: a comment sharing a line with code does not remove that line
test.purpose: A statement carrying a trailing comment still counts. Excluding by line rather than by byte deletes it, which an earlier implementation did.

test.name: HLR-016: inline syntax inside a block comment excludes no line twice
test.purpose: Comment-like openers inside a block comment do not cause any line to be excluded more than once.

test.name: HLR-020: a file of only comments reports zero ELOC
test.purpose: A file with nothing but comments reports zero, without error.

test.name: the hand-counted nesting totals match
test.purpose: The physical line count, the file's ELOC, and the function count match the fixture's hand-counted header.

test.name: HLR-068: the innermost function owns its own statements
test.purpose: Each nested function reports the statements written inside it.

test.name: HLR-068: the innermost function owns its own decision points
test.purpose: Each nested function reports the branches written inside it; running the query against each body without attribution would give an enclosing function everything its nested functions branch on.

test.name: HLR-017: complexity is one plus the decision points
test.purpose: The outermost function scores one plus its two decision points — the `if` and the `&&` short-circuiting inside its condition.

test.name: HLR-068: an enclosing function gains none of the nested one's lines
test.purpose: The outermost function reports its own three statements and none of the five in the file. Attributing to the outermost enclosing function would report five; attributing to every enclosing one would report five, two, and one.

test.name: HLR-067: all three functions are reported in their own right
test.purpose: Three levels of nesting yield three reported functions, not one.

test.name: HLR-019: the file counts each statement line once
test.purpose: The file's ELOC is the number of distinct lines carrying a statement, however those statements are attributed.

test.name: HLR-032: nested attribution is deterministic across runs
test.purpose: Repeating the run produces identical bytes, so the attribution does not depend on the order the query matched.

test.name: HLR-067: Ada reports a nested subprogram in its own right
test.purpose: Three subprograms nested three deep are three reported functions, which is the shape HLR-067 was written for.

test.name: HLR-068: an Ada subprogram gains none of its nested ones' work
test.purpose: Each of the three owns exactly its own ELOC and complexity; attributing to the outermost would give the outer one everything and the others nothing.

test.name: HLR-018: a Rust closure is not reported as a function
test.purpose: A closure has no name to report, so the report names the two `fn` items and not the closure beside them.

test.name: HLR-018: a Rust closure's decision point lands on the enclosing function
test.purpose: The enclosing function's complexity includes the closure's branch. Without the rule that branch would belong to nothing at all, since an unreported callable is not a function for it to land on — it would vanish from the report.

test.name: HLR-018: a Python lambda is not reported as a function
test.purpose: A lambda is unnamed and so is absent from the reported function set.

test.name: HLR-018: a Python lambda's conditional lands on the enclosing function
test.purpose: The conditional expression inside a lambda raises the enclosing function's complexity.

test.name: HLR-018: a C++ lambda is not reported as a function
test.purpose: A lambda is unnamed and so is absent from the reported function set.

test.name: HLR-018: a C++ lambda's conditional lands on the enclosing function
test.purpose: The conditional expression inside a lambda raises the enclosing function's complexity.

test.name: HLR-067: a nested named function is reported where a lambda is not
test.purpose: The distinction the two requirements draw, in one language and one function body: Rust's nested `fn` is reported and the closure beside it is not.

test.name: HLR-064: a path containing a comma does not split a record
test.purpose: Every row of the document parses to the same field count under an independent CSV reader, which a split field would break. The hostile value is a path rather than an identifier, because C cannot yet produce an identifier carrying a comma.

test.name: HLR-064: the path survives the round trip intact
test.purpose: The value read back out of the document is the value that went in, comma and quotes included.

test.name: HLR-064: a hostile path changes the field count of nothing
test.purpose: A record over a hostile path has the same number of fields as one over an ordinary path, so quoting preserved the structure rather than merely surviving it.

test.name: HLR-065: XML over a hostile path is well-formed
test.purpose: An independent parser accepts the document, so the escaping is correct rather than merely present.

test.name: HLR-065: the structural characters are escaped, not emitted raw
test.purpose: The angle brackets, ampersand, and quotation marks appear as entities in the document.

test.name: HLR-065: the path arrives intact after unescaping
test.purpose: An independent parser recovers the original value, so escaping and the document's meaning agree.

test.name: HLR-056: a hostile path survives a record round trip
test.purpose: Regeneration over a hostile path matches a direct run. An asymmetry — escaped on the way out and not unescaped on the way in — passes a well-formedness check and still corrupts the report.

test.name: HLR-027: the table renders a hostile path unchanged
test.purpose: The aligned table escapes nothing and must not: it is read by a person, and a path is what it is.

test.name: HLR-014: a template specialisation is reported under its full name
test.purpose: An explicit specialisation names itself with its template arguments, so the reported name carries a comma and two angle brackets — an identifier the analyser produces rather than one the suite constructs.

test.name: HLR-064: an identifier containing a comma stays one CSV field
test.purpose: Every row parses to the same field count under an independent reader, and the name reads back whole. This is the value HLR-064 was written for, reachable only once C++ shipped.

test.name: HLR-065: an identifier containing angle brackets is escaped
test.purpose: The angle brackets appear as entities, never raw, so no identifier can open or close a tag.

test.name: HLR-065: XML carrying such an identifier is well-formed
test.purpose: An independent parser accepts the document, so the escaping is correct rather than merely present.

test.name: HLR-056: such an identifier survives a record round trip
test.purpose: Regeneration matches a direct run, so escaping on the way out and reading on the way in agree about the identifier.

test.name: the hand-counted subject totals match
test.purpose: The subject's totals match the values in the fixture's header, so a later failure is about the round trip rather than about the subject having changed.

test.name: HLR-056: regenerated Markdown is byte-identical to a direct run
test.purpose: The report rebuilt from a record is identical to the one a direct analysis produces at the same threshold — not similar, identical, so a diff of the two is empty.

test.name: HLR-057: the threshold supplied now is the one applied
test.purpose: Regeneration at a given threshold matches a direct run at that threshold, so the threshold reaches the rebuilt report.

test.name: HLR-057: the same record at two thresholds gives two listings
test.purpose: Two thresholds over one record produce different reports. Without this, the test above would pass for a build that ignored the threshold entirely.

test.name: HLR-055: regeneration reads no source file
test.purpose: A report is produced from the record with the working directory elsewhere and the source unreachable.

test.name: HLR-054: the record carries every tier the report presents
test.purpose: Every tier the report has today appears in the record — the totals, the languages, the files and their functions, and the skipped list. A tier missing here regenerates as a report that looks complete and is not.

test.name: HLR-061: the record carries a format-version identifier
test.purpose: The record identifies the structure it uses, exactly once.

test.name: HLR-058: input that is not XML is rejected with no output
test.purpose: A file that is not XML is rejected with the fatal status and nothing on the results stream.

test.name: HLR-058: a well-formed document of another shape is rejected
test.purpose: Being parseable is not being an elc record; no best-effort partial conversion is attempted.

test.name: HLR-058: an unsupported format version is rejected, naming it
test.purpose: A bumped version is rejected, and the diagnostic names both the version found and the version this build reads.

test.name: HLR-058: a truncated record is rejected
test.purpose: A record whose root never closes is rejected rather than read as far as it goes.

test.name: HLR-058: an absent record is rejected
test.purpose: A record that cannot be opened is a rejection rather than a crash.

test.name: HLR-055: regeneration defaults to Markdown without being asked
test.purpose: The mode's output format is its default, so it is usable without a redundant option.

test.name: HLR-063: a format other than Markdown is rejected in regeneration mode
test.purpose: A saved record carries the findings of a run rather than the graph, so another format is a usage error rather than a silently ignored request.

test.name: HLR-063: an explicit Markdown selection is accepted
test.purpose: Saying the default out loud is not an error; only asking for something else is.

test.name: HLR-063: a target alongside --from-xml is a usage error
test.purpose: The record is the input; a target would name a second source of truth for one report.

test.name: HLR-122: regeneration writes no .dot, default-on though it is
test.purpose: A record carries the findings of a run rather than the topology they were drawn from, so the default-on companion is simply not produced. Nothing was requested, so declining silently is what the requirement asks for.

test.name: LLR-CLI-15: an explicit companion request with --from-xml is rejected
test.purpose: An explicit request is a usage error rather than a silently ignored one, so a user who asked for a file and got none is told why instead of discovering the absence.

test.name: LLR-CLI-15: declining a companion alongside --from-xml is not an error
test.purpose: The boundary of the rule above: --no-dot is a refusal rather than a request, and refusing something that was never going to be produced conflicts with nothing.

test.name: an intact runtime analyses the subject
test.purpose: The control the rest of the group is read against: an unbroken runtime directory analyses the subject and reports its function.

test.name: HLR-036: an absent runtime directory is fatal before any file is read
test.purpose: A missing runtime location ends the run with no report, since no analysis is possible in that state.

test.name: HLR-036: a runtime location that is a file is fatal
test.purpose: The same unusable state reached differently is treated the same way.

test.name: HLR-036: an absent extension map is fatal
test.purpose: Without the extension map nothing can be routed to a language, which is the fatal state.

test.name: HLR-036: an extension map naming no language is fatal
test.purpose: A map present but naming nothing is as unusable as one that is missing.

test.name: HLR-036: a fatal runtime failure is diagnosed on stderr
test.purpose: The fatal diagnostic names the location and reaches the diagnostic stream.

test.name: HLR-070: an absent grammar degrades that language only
test.purpose: A language whose grammar is missing is excluded, the run completes, the status stays 0, and the affected file is listed as skipped.

test.name: HLR-070: a grammar exposing no entry point degrades that language only
test.purpose: A shared object that loads but exposes no grammar entry point is unusable rather than fatal.

test.name: HLR-070: a grammar that is not a shared object degrades that language only
test.purpose: A parser file that cannot be loaded at all is unusable rather than fatal.

test.name: HLR-121: a module missing a required query file is unusable, not undefined
test.purpose: A module omitting one of the six required query files is handled under HLR-070 rather than producing undefined behaviour.

test.name: HLR-070: an unparseable query degrades that language only
test.purpose: A query file that will not compile excludes its language and leaves the run otherwise intact.

test.name: HLR-070: the diagnostic names the language and the reason
test.purpose: The diagnostic identifies the language, the query file, and the reason in words rather than as a numeric code.

test.name: HLR-070: an unusable module is reported once, not once per file
test.purpose: The load failure is diagnosed once for the language rather than once for every file that would have used it.

test.name: HLR-059: the environment variable takes precedence over the adjacent runtime
test.purpose: Pointing the environment variable at a broken runtime degrades the run even though a working one sits beside the executable, which it can only do if the variable was preferred.

test.name: HLR-059: the runtime adjacent to the executable is used when the variable is unset
test.purpose: With the variable unset, the runtime beside the executable is found and used.

test.name: HLR-059: an installed elc finds the runtime under share/elc
test.purpose: A binary installed into a staging root analyses a file with no environment variable set. The build tree flatters the adjacent path with a symlink beside the binary, so this is the only level at which the installed layout is exercised at all — and it failed outright before the resolver tried the second path.

test.name: HLR-059: the install puts the runtime where the binary looks for it
test.purpose: The staged layout is asserted directly, so a regression names the disagreement between the install target and the resolver rather than only its symptom, and so that moving the runtime into the binary's own directory would fail rather than pass.

test.name: HLR-059: the environment variable still wins over the installed layout
test.purpose: The variable takes precedence over a runtime the installed layout would otherwise have found, as it does over the adjacent one.

test.name: HLR-036: a binary with no runtime anywhere names every path it tried
test.purpose: The diagnostic lists each candidate and the variable that overrides them. The message it replaced quoted one path no layout uses, sending the reader to look for a runtime directory inside a directory of executables.

test.name: the walk yields exactly the three source files
test.purpose: The analysed file set for the hand-counted traversal tree is exactly the three files its header states, and nothing else.

test.name: the hand-counted traversal totals match
test.purpose: The file count and physical line total match the values counted by hand in the fixture's header.

test.name: HLR-005: a binary extension is excluded
test.purpose: A file whose extension appears in the runtime exclusion list is absent from the walk's result.

test.name: HLR-005: a hidden directory is excluded
test.purpose: The contents of a hidden directory are absent from the walk's result.

test.name: HLR-005: a hidden file is excluded
test.purpose: A hidden file in the target is absent from the walk's result, which is what makes a configuration-like file planted there unable to change the output.

test.name: HLR-069: a symbolic link is not followed during the walk
test.purpose: A link to a file already inside the tree is not followed, so the file it names is not contributed a second time.

test.name: HLR-069: a cyclic directory link does not hang the walk
test.purpose: A self-referential directory link is not descended into and the walk terminates with the expected file set.

test.name: HLR-069: a symbolic link named as a target is resolved
test.purpose: A link named directly as a target is resolved and its referent analysed, the other half of the symbolic-link policy.

test.name: HLR-072: naming a file and its directory analyses it once
test.purpose: Overlapping targets over the fixture tree yield the same file set as the directory alone.

test.name: HLR-071: several targets combine into one report
test.purpose: Two targets produce a single report spanning both.

test.name: HLR-043: the fixture tree is unchanged by a run
test.purpose: Every file in the fixture tree checksums identically before and after a run.

test.name: HLR-137: statements after a return are reported
test.purpose: The statements following a return in the same block are reported, with their line ranges.

test.name: HLR-138: a label following a return is NOT reported
test.purpose: A labeled_statement is a sibling of the return and is reachable. Reporting it would invite deleting a live goto target, and the count is taken against the extracted rows rather than the whole output so the assertion cannot pass vacuously.

test.name: HLR-137: statements after a break are reported
test.purpose: A break terminates its block for the sibling walk exactly as a return does.

test.name: HLR-137: statements after a continue are reported
test.purpose: A continue terminates its block for the sibling walk exactly as a return does.

test.name: LLR-DED-01: the walk does not leave the terminator's own block
test.purpose: A statement after the loop containing the break is live: the walk visits siblings within one parent and does not climb.

test.name: HLR-138: a switch arm does not leak into the next
test.purpose: In this grammar a case construct contains the statements of its arm, so a return in one arm has no sibling to leak into and the following case is not reported.

test.name: LLR-DED-01: a statement following two terminators is reported once
test.purpose: A statement the walk reaches from two terminators appears once, so the report does not depend on how many ways it was found.

test.name: HLR-137: the consequence of if (0) and the else of if (1) are reported
test.purpose: Both literal-condition shapes are found, each as its whole span.

test.name: HLR-137: the body of a literally false loop is reported
test.purpose: A loop whose condition is written as a false literal has an unreachable body.

test.name: HLR-138: a do-while(0) body is NOT reported
test.purpose: A do-while body runs exactly once, and it is one of the commonest idioms in C. Reporting it would be a false claim against ordinary code.

test.name: HLR-138: a branch guarded by a variable is NOT reported
test.purpose: Neither a plain variable nor a const one holding zero makes its branch dead: deciding either needs data flow, and elc performs none.

test.name: LLR-DED-03: a zero the source did not write as one is undecided
test.purpose: Hexadecimal and octal zeroes fall through as undecided rather than being judged, while the decimal zero beside them is reported — the contrast being what shows the query is narrow rather than merely quiet.

test.name: HLR-137: the two causes are distinguished
test.purpose: A statement after a terminator and a branch under a literal condition are reported with different causes, because the reader's next action differs.

test.name: HLR-016: a comment is not dead code
test.purpose: A comment is a named sibling, so without the merged-comment exclusion the walk would report the trailing note on the terminator's own line. The exact row count pins it.

test.name: HLR-139: a language supplying a dead-code query reports every language analysed
test.purpose: The section heading states that nothing was left unanalysed, so an empty table means none found.

test.name: HLR-139: a language with no dead-code query is reported not analysed
test.purpose: Ada ships without one on purpose, and the heading names it rather than leaving a clean-looking table.

test.name: HLR-139: removing a query file makes that language unanalysed, not clean
test.purpose: The same distinction against a language that does ship one: with the file removed the findings vanish and the heading says the analysis was not performed.

test.name: HLR-070: a module missing an optional query is still usable
test.purpose: Every other measurement survives the absence of an optional query file, which is the whole point of the file being optional.

test.name: HLR-070: an optional query that will not compile is a defect, not a choice
test.purpose: An optional file that is present and will not compile is diagnosed like a required one. Omitting a file is a decision the contract allows; writing a broken one is not.

test.name: HLR-137: dead statements inside an unreachable function are still reported
test.purpose: Neither dead-code analysis suppresses the other: the function is reported unreachable by traversal and its dead statement is reported by syntax in the same run.

test.name: HLR-139: dead code is found in every language supplying a query
test.purpose: Python, Rust and C++ each find the statement after a terminator, so the mechanism is not C's alone.

test.name: HLR-138: no language claims a branch guarded by a variable
test.purpose: The restraint holds in Python and Rust as it does in C: no language module is permitted to infer a value.

test.name: HLR-097: a clique of unused functions calling one another is reported
test.purpose: The case textual linters get wrong. Each of the pair has a caller, so a no-caller rule finds neither; traversal reaches neither from any root.

test.name: HLR-096: a function reachable only through an address-taken pointer is NOT reported
test.purpose: A function appearing only as an initialiser of a vector table is a root, and reporting it dead would tell a user to delete an interrupt handler.

test.name: LLR-RTS-02: an address-taken function is a root, not merely an exception
test.purpose: A function called only from an address-taken one is reachable through it. An implementation that excluded address-taken functions from the report without traversing from them would report it dead.

test.name: HLR-096: functions reached from the declared entry point are not reported
test.purpose: The declared root and what it calls are absent from the unreachable list.

test.name: HLR-115: with no entry points declared, nothing is reported unreachable
test.purpose: The list is empty and the heading states the omission and its reason, rather than reporting the whole program dead.

test.name: HLR-115: a declared entry point matching nothing says so differently
test.purpose: The two absences carry different headings, because they call for different actions from the reader.

test.name: LLR-CTR-09: omitting reachability does not omit its neighbours
test.purpose: A run with no entry points still reports its global-access map.

test.name: HLR-096: a global touched only by unreachable functions is unreachable
test.purpose: The storage goes the way of the code that touches it.

test.name: LLR-UGL-01: a global a reachable function touches is not condemned
test.purpose: One live accessor is enough to keep an object out of the unreachable list.

test.name: HLR-115: with no entry points, no global is reported unreachable either
test.purpose: The data half of the analysis is omitted with the function half, rather than condemning every object.

test.name: HLR-091: every global reports its writers and its readers
test.purpose: Both sets are present for every object, whether or not the object carries a finding.

test.name: HLR-092: a global touched by one function is flagged for scope reduction
test.purpose: The finding appears with its published source, for the object no state edge exists for.

test.name: HLR-093: a global spanning disconnected regions is a hidden channel
test.purpose: The finding names the disconnected participants, grouped by region, because the grouping is the finding.

test.name: HLR-093: shared state within one call-connected region is not a channel
test.purpose: An object shared across a call edge carries no finding at all, asserted on the row rather than on the output — which does carry both phrases for the other objects.

test.name: LLR-GLB-04: both findings carry their published source
test.purpose: Each of the two verdicts is attributed to MISRA C Rule 8.9 in the report.

test.name: HLR-094: a call crossing a declared scope boundary is reported
test.purpose: A call from one declared scope into another appears as a crossing naming both ends.

test.name: HLR-094: a shared global crossing a boundary is reported too
test.purpose: A scope sharing a variable with another without calling it has not been isolated, and the crossing names the object.

test.name: HLR-094: exactly the two crossings are reported
test.purpose: The count in the heading matches the rows, so neither kind is reported twice nor an intra-scope edge counted.

test.name: HLR-115: with no scopes declared the analysis is omitted with a reason
test.purpose: The heading states the omission rather than leaving an empty table to be read as isolation verified.

test.name: HLR-094: an edge within one scope is not a crossing
test.purpose: The same calls and the same shared variable, with both files in one declared scope, produce nothing.

test.name: HLR-094: a file matching no declaration is outside the partition
test.purpose: A file no declaration names lies outside the partition rather than in a scope of its own.

test.name: HLR-063: a malformed scope declaration is a usage error
test.purpose: A declaration that cannot be parsed ends the run with the fatal status and a diagnostic, rather than becoming a scope matching nothing.

test.name: HLR-032: the state sections survive a record round trip byte-identically
